scope: DECISIVE EVIDENCE: at state 10 with count = 1 the frame is still a BLACK SCREEN with a loading spinner in the bottom-right corner

the_capture.method: tools/capture_screen.ps1 (a real desktop grab, because PrintWindow returns black for this D3D client)

what_the_image_shows: there is a single small circular loading indicator at the bottom-right corner
that is the same loading-screen presentation the user has been reporting: map loading, waiting for other players, loading player data, black load
why_this_matters_more_than_the_state_num: the network state variable reads 10 and the client holds one entity - by the project's long-standing oracle that combination meant 'in match'
the screenshot shows that it does not: the client is still on a loading screen
so state 10 is a NETWORK-layer value and does not imply that cgame has entered the world
and every earlier conclusion that used state 10 as success inherits that limitation - the same class of error as treating state 10 as proof of a parsed snapshot
what_the_spinner_tells_us: the client is still waiting on a condition it has not received
the candidates are the ones already suspected: map-load completion, a clientNum/view-entity tie, or a specific configstring
the spinner is the real acceptance signal to chase, not the state variable
the_practical_redirect: stop using state == 10 as an oracle; use the screenshot (black-with-spinner vs a rendered world)
and find what the spinner waits on - the most direct probe is the loading-screen text or the condition the frontend checks before switching to the world
